title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a base scheme. M is a rank-4 Azumaya algebra over S, typically M = End_{O_S}(F) with F locally free of rank 2. The groups are G = M^* (a form of GL2), SG (norm 1, a form of SL2) and PG = G/G_m (a form of PGL2). On the previous page an 'elementary projector' is a section P of M with det P = 0 and Tr P = 1. Equivalently, P is locally the matrix diag(0,1) for a basis e0, e1. Its kernel D0 and image D1 are line subbundles with F = D0 ⊕ D1.

This page makes explicit the bijection, stated in the Corollary, between elementary projectors and Killing pairs (T, B), i.e. a maximal torus contained in a Borel.
- The torus is T = A_P^*, the units of the commutative rank-2 subalgebra A_P = O_S[P] ≅ O_S × O_S. It is the diagonal torus diag(μ0, μ1).
- The Borel is B0, the stabilizer of the flag D0 ⊂ F. In the adapted basis it is the upper-triangular group, formula (13).
- The opposite Killing pair is (T, B1), where B1 is lower-triangular, formula (14). Intrinsically B1 is the stabilizer of D1.
- The projector associated with (T, B1) is the complementary projector, written '1−N' but meaning 1−P.

Remarks: count of moduli schemes over the scheme ℙ of Borels (ℙ = ℙ(F), a P^1-bundle over S; the same for G, SG and PG).
- The scheme of elementary unipotents ε = 1+N (N square-zero, nonzero in every fibre) is a G_m-torsor over ℙ, called 'droites épinglées'. Given the Borel, i.e. the line D = ker N = im N, N is a nowhere-vanishing section of the line bundle Hom(F/D, D). This scheme is smooth of relative dimension 2 over S.
- The scheme of elementary projectors is isomorphic to the scheme of Killing pairs. It is smooth of relative dimension 1 over ℙ, the fibre being the tori in a fixed Borel, a torsor under the unipotent radical ≅ G_a. Its total relative dimension over S is 2, which is the dimension of the orbit GL2/T.
- The fibre product over ℙ of these two schemes (Borel + torus + nonzero root vector) is the scheme of pinnings (épinglages). These are isomorphisms GL(2)_S ≅ G, SL(2)_S ≅ SG or PGL(2)_S ≅ PG compatible with the standard pinning. It is a torsor of relative dimension 3 under PGL(2).
- The next page continues: ε and P are called 'associated' when they come from one pinning, which gives PN = 0, NP = N. It then turns to the conjugacy invariant Tr²/det for sections of PG.

Purpose: this is elementary bookkeeping on forms of GL2/PGL2 over an arbitrary base (SGA3 language), in preparation for classifying conjugacy classes of sections of PG. It belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' within the Teichmüller-tower / Galois–Teichmüller programme.
errors: 'Le proj. él. associé au couple de Killing opposé (T,B1) est 1−N': N is not yet defined here and is later used for the nilpotent ε−1. The intended statement is that the opposite pair corresponds to 1−P (kernel and image exchanged). This is a notational slip.

On the next page Grothendieck writes Aut_{S-gr}(GL(2)_S) ≅ PGL(2)_S. This is false as stated: GL2 has the outer automorphism g ↦ det(g)^{-1} g, which inverts the centre. It is true for SL2 and PGL2. The pinning torsor is nonetheless a PGL2-torsor if one restricts to isomorphisms of Azumaya algebras / pinned isomorphisms. This error is on the neighbouring page, not this one.

ideas.what: Bijection between elementary projectors (det 0, trace 1) in a rank-4 Azumaya algebra and Killing pairs (maximal torus ⊂ Borel) in the associated forms of GL2/SL2/PGL2. The torus is the units of O_S[P]; the Borel is the stabilizer of ker P; opposite pair ↔ 1−P.
ideas.modern_name: Killing pairs / Borel–torus pairs in reductive group schemes of rank 1; idempotents of quaternion (Azumaya) algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Demazure–Grothendieck, SGA3 (couples de Killing, Exp. XXII–XXIV); classical for split algebras
ideas.where_published: SGA3 (terminology 'couple de Killing', épinglages); this explicit rank-1 dictionary is routine

ideas.what: Fibration picture over the scheme of Borels: elementary unipotents form a G_m-torsor over ℙ (relative dim 2 over S); projectors/Killing pairs form an affine-line torsor over ℙ; their fibre product over ℙ is the PGL2-torsor of pinnings.
ideas.modern_name: Scheme of pinnings as torsor under the adjoint group; regular nilpotent orbit as G_m-torsor over the flag variety
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA3 (Demazure), standard structure theory of reductive group schemes
ideas.where_published: SGA3 Exp. XXIII–XXIV (épinglages, schéma des épinglages)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard rank-one structure theory (SGA3 language) over a general base, written out explicitly as preparation for a conjugacy classification in PGL2. Nothing here appears new or absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Le schéma des E_1' should read 'Le schéma des ε' (the elementary unipotents ε = 1+N).
In 'associant à P le tore T = A_P^*' the struck-out letter before P is a deletion; the subscript is P (the projector), not a prime 𝔭.

The interlinear insertion near 'est un fibré' is largely illegible; the word read as 'Nuils[?]' should be marked illegible rather than transcribed as 'Nuils'. The main sense is 'fibré en droites épointées/épinglées (i.e. un G_m-torseur)'.
'est 1−N' is what is written, but it denotes the complementary projector 1−P.
The page number at the top ('975'?) is uncertain.
